name: Vercel
description: Vercel is the premier deployment platform for Next.js, React, and frontend frameworks. It provides git-based deployments, instant preview URLs per pull request, a global edge network, and serverless functions — shipping from `git push` to production in seconds.

useCases.task: Deploy a Next.js application to production
Add serverless API routes to a frontend app
Set up preview deployments for every pull request
Deploy a static site with global CDN

setupSteps: Create a new project from the dashboard
Connect your GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket repository
Vercel auto-deploys on every push to your default branch
Generate an API token at vercel.com/account/tokens and set VERCEL_TOKEN

pricing.freeTier: Hobby plan: unlimited personal projects, 100GB bandwidth/month, 100GB-hours serverless function execution
pricing.costPer: Pro: $40/month for 2 seats, $20/seat thereafter. Additional bandwidth at $0.15/GB above included.

rateLimits.limit: 100GB bandwidth/month, 100GB-hours serverless execution, 6000 build minutes/month, 12 serverless function regions
rateLimits.notes: Serverless functions time out at 10 seconds on the Hobby plan and up to 300 seconds on Pro/Enterprise. Build concurrency is limited to 1 concurrent build on Hobby.
rateLimits.retryStrategy: Functions have 10s (Hobby) or 60s (Pro) timeout. Handle timeout errors with retry logic in client.

codeExamples.title: Deploy via CLI (most common)
codeExamples.notes: Install the Vercel CLI globally with `npm i -g vercel` for one-off deploys. Use `vercel --prod` to deploy to production. The @vercel/sdk is best for programmatic automation — CI pipelines, deployment dashboards, or listing/cancelling deployments.

codeExamples.title: Create a serverless API route (Next.js)
codeExamples.notes: Placing a file at app/api/*/route.ts automatically becomes a serverless function on Vercel. Set `export const runtime = 'edge'` to run on the global edge network instead of a single region. Edge functions have a 25MB memory limit vs 1GB for standard serverless functions.

gotchas: Hobby plan users cannot attach custom domains to production deployments on personal projects — all personal deployments are served from *.vercel.app subdomains only. A Vercel Pro or Teams plan is required to use a custom domain on a team project.

Serverless functions on the Hobby plan have a hard 10-second execution timeout that cannot be configured. Functions that call slow third-party APIs, run LLM inference, or process large files will be killed at 10 seconds. Upgrading to Pro unlocks up to 300 seconds.

Each git push to any branch triggers a new deployment — there is no staging environment by default. Use Vercel's built-in Environment targeting (Preview vs Production) and configure branch-to-environment mappings explicitly to avoid accidentally shipping preview code to production.

Environment variables are scoped per environment (Development, Preview, Production) and must be configured separately for each. A variable added to the Preview environment does NOT automatically appear in Production — forgetting this is a common source of 'undefined env var' bugs after promotion to production.

reliability.uptimeGuarantee: 99.99% uptime SLA on Pro and Enterprise plans
reliability.notes: Vercel runs on a multi-region edge network with automatic failover. Static assets and edge functions are distributed globally via Anycast. Serverless function regions are user-selectable on Pro.

qualityJustification: Industry standard for Next.js and React deployments. Git push to deploy, instant previews per PR, and a global edge network make it the fastest path from code to production. Serverless functions are first-class citizens.
bestFor: Deploying Next.js, React, and other frontend frameworks with zero-config git deployments, preview environments, and serverless functions
